government.note: Government type as on 1 January 2000: Ba'athist Syria. President Hafez al-Assad (in office since 12 March 1971) led the Ba'ath Party (Syria Region), which headed the National Progressive Front of partner parties; the People's Council (250 seats) was elected on 30 November - 1 December 1998 with 135 seats for the Ba'ath Party, 32 for its front partners and 83 for independents. Stages after 2000, as dated facts (Wikipedia, List of heads of state of Syria and List of prime ministers of Syria): Hafez al-Assad died on 10 June 2000; Vice President Abdul Halim Khaddam was Acting President until 17 July 2000, when his son Bashar al-Assad took office. The Syrian civil war followed the 2011 uprising. Bashar al-Assad was deposed on 8 December 2024 (the fall of the Assad government). Ahmed al-Sharaa, leader of Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham, was de facto leader of Syria from 8 December 2024 and was appointed President of Syria for the transitional period by the Syrian General Command on 29 January 2025; on that date the 2024 People's Assembly was dissolved and replaced by an interim legislative council, and the Ba'ath Party and the National Progressive Front parties were dissolved. A caretaker government under Prime Minister Mohammed al-Bashir ran from 10 December 2024 to 29 March 2025, when the transitional government was formed and the post of Prime Minister was abolished. The Constitutional Declaration of March 2025 re-established the People's Assembly; its 140 elected members were chosen by electoral colleges from 5 October 2025 and 70 members were appointed by the President (announced 1 July 2026), and it first met on 12 July 2026. Presidential referendums (for example in 2000) are not modelled in the light tier. The type field keeps the 2000 value.

offices.note: Under the 1973 constitution the President was nominated by the People's Council and confirmed in a referendum (not fetched; see the light-tier note). Since 29 January 2025 the office is held under the transitional arrangements and the Constitutional Declaration.

system.note: 2000: 250 seats elected on 30 November - 1 December 1998 in multi-member constituencies (Wikipedia: the assembly was previously elected by direct popular vote in multi-member constituencies; the Ba'ath Party and its allies held about two thirds of the seats). seats_2000 is that result: Ba'ath 135, Arab Socialist Union Party 7, Socialist Unionist Party 7 and other front partners 18 (Syrian Communist Party 8, Arab Socialist Movement 4, Democratic Socialist Unionist Party 4, Arab Democratic Union Party 2), independents 83. Since 2025 the chamber is the 210-seat People's Assembly: 140 members chosen by electoral colleges from 5 October 2025 (indirect, hierarchical voting) and 70 appointed by the President, with a 30-month term; the 2025 election is recorded in elections.json.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate only: no competitive national vote had been held, and no vote shares were published for the 1998 election (135 of 250 seats went to the Ba'ath Party, 32 to National Progressive Front partners and 83 to independents). The weights are a gameplay estimate: baathist = Ba'ath Party and its supporters in the state, army and administration; statist = Nasserist and other front partners; marxist_leninist = the communist partners; islamist and islamic_democrat = religious-conservative and moderate Islamic currents outside the legal party system; regionalist = Kurdish communities; tribal_traditional = tribal and rural notables; centrist_liberal and big_tent = urban professionals and independents.
